name: WindowFilterModel::filterAcceptsRow
prose: Precondition: this is the const filter-model member (windowmodel.cpp:245); m_windowModel may be null; sourceRow/sourceParent index into the source model. Postcondition: returns false if m_windowModel is null or the source index (sourceRow, 0, sourceParent) is invalid; returns true if the index's data is an invalid QVariant (treated as valid data); returns false if the data's Window* is null or window->isClient() is false; then returns false if an activity filter is set and the window is not on that activity, if a desktop filter is set and the window is not on that desktop, if an output filter is set and window->output() differs, or if a window-type filter is set and the window's type mask has no bit in common with it. If the text filter m_filter is non-empty, it returns true when the caption, window role, resource name or resource class contains the filter case-insensitively and false otherwise (the minimized setting is not consulted in this case). Otherwise it returns !window->isMinimized() when m_showMinimizedWindows is false and true when it is true. No member is modified.

name: TabBox::keyPress
prose: Precondition: this TabBox is valid; keyEvent is a KeyboardKeyEvent. Postcondition: returns nothing. If m_tabGrab is false it returns at once with no state change. Otherwise it tests the shortcut pairs of the TABBOX_MODE_COUNT modes in cyclic order starting from the current mode (a collision keeps the current mode) with matchShortcuts. On the first mode that gives a non-Steady direction: if that mode differs from mode(), it calls accept(false) (activates the current client if one exists and, if that client is a desktop, toggles showing-desktop), calls setMode(testedMode), schedules a 50 ms single-shot that calls reset() and nextPrev(direction == Forward), and returns; if it equals mode(), the loop stops with that direction. If no mode matched (direction Steady): for Qt::Key_Escape it calls close(true) (removes the grab if grabbed, hide(true), clears m_tabGrab and m_noModifierGrab, updates the keyboard, re-enables pointer constraints); for any other key it builds a QKeyEvent(KeyPress, key, NoModifier) and passes it to grabbedKeyEvent; both then return. If a direction matched and keyEvent.state is Repeated, it returns without advancing when direction is Forward and the current row equals clientList().count() - 1 or direction is Backward and the current row is 0. Otherwise it calls KDEWalkThroughWindows(direction == Forward), which calls nextPrev(forward) and so setCurrentIndex plus tabBoxUpdated.
note: slice starts inside the file but the function head is present (tabbox.cpp:902-964). Checked all returns (906, 937, 950, 956, 958, end). Reviewer claim (auto-repeat at list boundary returns without advancing) is right and is stated.

name: MemoryMap::operator=(MemoryMap &&other)
prose: Precondition: *this and other may be in any state (valid mapping, MAP_FAILED, moved-from). Postcondition: if m_data != MAP_FAILED, munmap(m_data, m_size) is called on the old mapping; then m_data and m_size are taken from other with other.m_data set to MAP_FAILED and other.m_size set to 0, and *this is returned. For two distinct objects this leaves other empty and *this owning other's old mapping. Self-assignment (&other == this) is not handled: the mapping is unmapped by the munmap call and then m_data and m_size are re-assigned from their own old values, so the object keeps the stale (already unmapped) pointer and size and the destructor will later call munmap on that stale pointer again.
note: checked memorymap.h:43-51. Reviewer round 15 is right: std::exchange(other.m_data, MAP_FAILED) returns the old value which is then assigned back into the same member, so a self-move leaves a dangling pointer, not MAP_FAILED/0. Old prose wrong.

name: SurfaceInterfacePrivate::applyState
prose: Precondition: next is a non-null pointer to a valid SurfaceState (normally the pending state) and current is valid; q is the owning SurfaceInterface. Postcondition: before merging it records which changes happened (from next->committed and a comparison with current): bufferChanged and bufferReleasePointChanged when the Buffer field is committed and buffer/releasePoint differ, transformChanged when BufferTransform is committed and differs, visibilityChanged when Buffer is committed and bool(buffer) differs, colorDescription/yuvCoefficients change when committed and different, and the plain committed flags for opaque, shadow, blur, contrast, slide, subsurface order, presentation mode hint and alpha multiplier (those are flagged whenever committed, even if the value is the same). It saves the old surfaceSize, bufferSourceBox and inputRegion, calls next->mergeInto(current.get()) (which moves next's committed fields, frame callbacks, damage and buffer damage into current and clears next's committed mask, damage and buffer damage), sets bufferRef = current->buffer and, only if both a buffer and a release point exist, registers the release point on the buffer, resets presentationFeedback if there is no buffer, and sets scaleOverride = pendingScaleOverride. With a buffer it recomputes bufferSourceBox, surfaceSize (viewport destination size, else viewport source size, else the transformed buffer size over bufferScale), inputRegion (input & surface rect), opaqueRegion (the whole surface rect if the buffer has no alpha channel, else opaque & surface rect), and bufferDamage (buffer damage united with mapped damage, limited to the buffer rect), clears current's damage and bufferDamage, and, if scaleOverride != 1.0, scales and rounds out the opaque and input regions and divides surfaceSize by scaleOverride; without a buffer it sets size 0, empty source box, empty damage, input and opaque regions. It then emits signals: opaqueChanged when the opaque flag was committed; inputChanged when the input region differs; bufferTransformChanged; updateEffectiveMapped() (not a signal) when visibilityChanged; bufferSourceBoxChanged when the box differs; bufferChanged; sizeChanged when the size differs; shadowChanged, blurChanged, contrastChanged, slideOnShowHideChanged, childSubSurfacesChanged when committed; when the color description or rendering intent changed, or the YUV coefficients changed, it replaces current->colorDescription with withYuvCoefficients(coefficients, range) and emits colorDescriptionChanged; presentationModeHintChanged, bufferReleasePointChanged, alphaMultiplierChanged; damaged(bufferDamage) if non-empty. Finally parentApplyState() is called on every below and above subsurface of current, extension->applyState on every extension state, and committed() is emitted. The caller keeps ownership of both states.
note: checked surface.cpp:679-821 and mergeInto (surface.cpp:622-677). Slice cut the head; function is SurfaceInterfacePrivate::applyState. Reviewers: release-point (round 0), flags-emitted-even-if-unchanged (round 1) and yuvCoefficients (round 2) were all right about older wordings and are now stated.

name: Window::setupWindowManagementInterface
prose: Precondition: this Window is valid; waylandServer() is available. Postcondition: returns nothing. It returns immediately, changing nothing, if m_windowManagementInterface is already set or if waylandServer()->windowManagement() is null. Otherwise it creates a PlasmaWindowInterface with windowManagement()->createWindow(this, internalId()), fills it from the window's current state (title, active, fullscreen, keep above/below, maximized, minimized, demands attention, closeable/maximizable/minimizable/fullscreenable, application menu paths, icon, resource name and app id, skip taskbar/switcher, pid, resizable/movable, virtual-desktop-changeable true, no-border and can-set-no-border, exclude-from-capture, parent window, frame and client geometry), connects Window signals so later changes are pushed to it, connects its request signals (close, move, resize, fullscreen, minimized, maximized, keep above/below, demands attention, active (activates the window only when set is true), no-border, exclude-from-capture, enter/enter-new/leave virtual desktop, enter/leave activity, send-to-output) to Window actions, adds the window's virtual desktops then sets on-all-desktops, adds its activities, and finally stores the interface in m_windowManagementInterface. The Window deletes it only in destroyWindowManagementInterface (window.cpp:1922-1926).
note: slice cut the head: the real function is Window::setupWindowManagementInterface (window.cpp:1727-1920); createWindowManagementInterface does not exist. Two early returns at 1731 and 1735. Old prose invented a name and said 'm_windowManagementInterface is null' as a precondition, but the code handles the non-null case by returning.

name: Window::setKeepAbove
prose: Precondition: none; any bool b. Postcondition: b is replaced by rules()->checkKeepAbove(b). If the replaced value is true and rules()->checkKeepBelow(false) is false, setKeepBelow(false) is called, before the equality test, so it can change keep-below state even if keep-above does not change. If the value equals keepAbove(), the function then returns with no further change. Otherwise m_keepAbove is set, doSetKeepAbove() and updateLayer() are called, updateWindowRules(Rules::Above) is called and keepAboveChanged(m_keepAbove) is emitted.

name: X11Window::readUserTimeMapTimestamp
prose: Precondition: info is valid; if asn_data is non-null and info->userTime() is non-zero, asn_id must be non-null (it is dereferenced); asn_data may be null; session is true or false. Postcondition: let time = info->userTime(). If asn_data is non-null and time != 0 and asn_id->timestamp() != 0 and (time == 4294967295 or NET::timestampCompare(asn_id->timestamp(), time) > 0), time is replaced by asn_id->timestamp(). If the resulting time is not 4294967295 (including 0), it is returned. If it is 4294967295: when the active window (as an X11Window) exists and does not belong to the same application (RelaxedForActive), the function decides whether this is the first window of the application (for a transient window: first if the active window has this as transient, or this is group-transient and no main window matches the same-application predicate; for a non-transient window: first unless the workspace has another client matching the same-application predicate), and returns 0 if it is not the first window and the effective focus-stealing-prevention level is above None; otherwise, if session is true it returns 4294967295, else it returns readUserCreationTime() (which is 4294967295 when the property is missing). The function is const and acquires nothing.
note: checked x11window.cpp:4191-4272. Reviewer round 1 (asn_id may be null) is right as to the precondition; round 2 (ASN used only when ASN timestamp non-zero) is right and the guard is now stated.

name: X11Window::allowWindowActivation
prose: Precondition: time is an X timestamp or 4294967295 meaning unknown; focus_in says whether activation follows a FocusIn event; this is a valid window. Postcondition: returns a bool, by this order of checks: t = time, or userTime() when time is 4294967295; level = rules()->checkFSP(options->focusStealingPreventionLevel()); true if the session manager is Saving and level <= Medium; ac = the active window, or the last active window if focus_in and there is no active window; false if t == 0 and rules()->checkAcceptFocus(false) is false; protection = ac's checkFPP(Medium) or None when ac is null; true if level == None or protection == None; false if level == Extreme or protection == Extreme; true if ac is null or ac->isDesktop(); true if the window belongs to the same application as ac (RelaxedForActive) and protection < High; false if level > Medium and protection > Low; if t == 4294967295, true when level < Medium and protection < High, else false; otherwise NET::timestampCompare(t, ac->userTime()) >= 0. No state is changed.
note: checked x11window.cpp:4348-4429. Reviewer round 2 (session saving can return true even with t==0) is right and the order is now explicit; round 1 concerned the formal contract, now empty.

name: _gtk_accelerator_parse
prose: Precondition: accelerator should be a NUL-terminated string; accelerator_key and accelerator_mods are NULL or point to writable storage. Postcondition: returns nothing. First, each non-NULL output pointer is set to 0. If accelerator is NULL, g_return_if_fail returns at that point with both outputs 0. Otherwise it scans the string: modifier tokens <release>, <control>, <ctrl>, <ctl>, <shift>, <shft>, <alt>, <mod1> to <mod5>, <hyper>, <super> add the corresponding GDK mask (hyper and super both add GDK_MOD4_MASK), <meta> is consumed without adding a mask, and any other <...> token is skipped up to and including the next '>'. A string that does not start with '<' at the current position is treated as the key: if it begins with '0x' followed by two hex digits (a hex keycode, at least 4 chars) the function sets an error because it cannot store keycodes; otherwise keyval is _gdk_keyval_from_name of the whole rest of the string and an unknown name (GDK_KEY_VoidSymbol) sets an error. The rest of the string is consumed by the key. On error both results are set to 0; otherwise *accelerator_key is the keyval (0 if there was no key part) and *accelerator_mods the accumulated mask, each only when its pointer is non-NULL. An unterminated '<' makes the skip loop at lines 258-264 consume past the terminating NUL and leave len at -1, after which the outer while (len) loop continues reading beyond the string.
note: slice cut the head: real function is _gtk_accelerator_parse (gtkaccelparse_p.c:157-315). The out-of-bounds note is from tracing lines 258-264 with an input like "<"; checked by hand, not by running.

name: ibus_panel_impanel_navigate
prose: Precondition: impanel is a valid IBusPanelImpanel with a usable engineManager; when impanel->selected < 0 the bus is a valid IBusBus. Postcondition: returns nothing. If start is true, impanel->selected is set to -1 first (even if the function then returns early). If engineManager->length() < 2 it returns. Otherwise it picks engine_desc: ibus_bus_get_global_engine(bus) when selected < 0; engines()[selected] with an added reference when 0 <= selected < length(); null when selected >= length(). If engine_desc is null it uses engines()[0] with an added reference. (If engines()[0] is itself null the final else branch returns without changing selected.) It then calls engineManager->navigate(engine_desc, forward), sets impanel->selected to (int)getIndexByName(name) (that function returns length() when the name is not found, not -1), unrefs engine_desc, and calls ibus_panel_impanel_real_register_properties(impanel) only if 0 <= selected < length().
note: checked panel.cpp:126-160 and enginemanager.cpp:84-133. Reviewer round 15 right (engines()[0] fallback also covers selected >= length()); round 1 right (start resets selected before early return). Old prose said getIndexByName may give -1: wrong, it gives length().

name: Backend::parentPid
prose: Precondition: this is a Backend and pid is a process id. Postcondition: const function that builds a local KSysGuard::Processes table and calls updateOrAddProcess(pid). It returns -1 if no process object is found for pid. If the process's parentPid() is -1 it returns -1. Otherwise it updates the table with the parent pid and returns -1 if the parent process object is not found; returns parentProc->pid() if proc's cgroup is non-empty and equal to the parent's cgroup; and returns -1 otherwise. The table is destroyed on return and nothing is handed to the caller.

name: Attica::KdePlatformDependent::loadAccessToken
prose: Precondition: none beyond a constructed object. Postcondition: returns nothing. If KAccounts::accountsManager() is null it logs a debug message and returns. Otherwise, for each account id of type "opendesktop-rating": it logs, skips ids for which accountsManager->account(id) is null (with a warning), and for the others creates a KAccounts::GetCredentialsJob (child of the accounts manager) and connects its finished signal to a lambda. When a job finishes, the lambda reads the IdToken from the credentials; if empty it logs a warning and leaves m_accessToken unchanged; otherwise it sets m_accessToken to the token and emits readyChanged(). The function itself does not wait for the jobs, so m_accessToken is changed later, by whichever job finishes with a non-empty token, with the last such job winning.

name: mouseKeysShortcut
prose: Precondition: display is a valid X Display pointer. Postcondition: returns a QString. It returns an empty string if neither XK_MouseKeys_Enable nor XK_Pointer_EnableKeys maps to a non-zero keycode, if XkbGetMap fails, or if the chosen keysym is not found in the key's groups/levels (the Xkb map is freed before the last of these returns). Otherwise it takes the modifier mask of the first active type-map entry matching the keysym's level, builds the key name from KKeyServer::xEventToQt and QKeySequence(key).toString(), and prepends modifier names in this order of prepending: AltGraph, Hyper, Super, the translated word "Meta" (when the Meta/Win modifier is set), the Qt::META key-sequence text (same condition), Alt, Ctrl, Shift, each followed by '+', when the corresponding bit is in the found modifier mask (AltGr/Meta/Super/Hyper masks computed from Xkb with the bits of the other modifiers removed). The returned string is that name.

name: KAccessConfig::launchOrcaConfiguration
prose: Precondition: none. Postcondition: returns nothing. It runs QProcess::execute("gsettings", {"set", "org.gnome.desktop.a11y.applications", "screen-reader-enabled", "true"}) and waits for it. If the return value is non-zero (including the not-started and crashed codes) it sets the orca launch feedback to an error text naming that command and returns without starting orca. Otherwise it calls QProcess::startDetached("orca", {"--setup"}, QString(), &pid) and, if that returns false, sets the feedback to the text 'Error: Could not launch "orca --setup"'. On success the pid is only stored in a local variable and no feedback is set or cleared.

name: DeviceModel::data
prose: Precondition: this is the const model; index belongs to it. For a child index, the settings must hold device info for the UDI (the Q_ASSERT at line 289 only checks this in debug builds). Postcondition: returns an empty QVariant for an invalid index. For a top-level index (no parent): DisplayRole in column 0 gives the row text for rows RowAll ("All Devices" or "All Known Devices" depending on automountUnknownDevices), RowAttached and RowDetached; CheckStateRole for row RowAll gives Qt::Checked/Unchecked from automountOnLogin in column 1 and automountOnPlugin in column 2; every other top-level combination gives an empty QVariant. For a child index: an empty QVariant if the parent row is above RowDetached, the column is >= columnCount() (3) or the row is >= rowCount(parent) (this includes all children of RowAll, whose rowCount is 0). Otherwise TypeRole gives Attached or Detached by the parent row, Qt::UserRole gives the UDI string, and then by column: column 0 gives for attached devices the Solid description (DisplayRole), the text "UDI: ..." (ToolTipRole) or the Solid icon (DecorationRole), and for detached devices the stored name, tooltip and stored icon; column 1 gives CheckStateRole as Checked/Unchecked from shouldAutomountDevice(udi, Login) and a login tooltip; column 2 gives the same for Attach; any other role/column combination gives an empty QVariant. No state is modified.

name: ref_main
prose: Precondition: argc/argv are as passed to main; the function parses its own options (getopt with "HLPRfhvx") into local flags. Postcondition: it never returns normally: every exit is exit(rval) or a call that exits. ref_usage() (prints usage and exit(1)) is called for an unknown option or when fewer than two arguments remain after the options. With -R and -h together it calls errx(1). The flags argument is parsed as octal if it starts with a digit '0'..'7' (err(1) if errno is set or the value is negative, errx(1) if trailing characters remain) and otherwise as symbolic flags with strtofflags (errx(1) if it fails). It then calls fts_open on the remaining files (err(1) if NULL) and loops with fts_read: FTS_D entries are skipped when -R is not given and otherwise processed at the post-order visit; FTS_DNR sets rval = 1 after a warning and still falls through to the flag change; FTS_ERR and FTS_NS warn, set rval = 1 and continue; each other entry gets newflags = the octal value, or (st_flags | set) & clear, is skipped if equal to the current flags, and otherwise chflagsat is called; a failure sets rval = 1 and warns unless -f, and a success prints the path (and old/new flags at -vv or on SIGINFO) when -v or SIGINFO. If errno is non-zero after the loop it calls err(1, "fts_read"). Otherwise it calls exit(rval), which is 0 unless some FTS error occurred or a chflagsat failed without -f.
note: slice cut the head: real function is ref_main (oracle.c:203-355). Old prose said the option globals were already set by option parsing; they are locals set by getopt in this function.

name: ref_pop_undo_stack
prose: Precondition: u_p is the number of valid entries in ustack; each entry has type UADD, UDEL, UMOV or VMOV and each UMOV/VMOV entry has its partner at the next lower index. Postcondition: if u_current_addr == -1 or u_addr_last == -1 it sets errmsg to "nothing to undo" and returns ERR with no other change. Otherwise: modified is set to 1 only when u_p != 0; get_addressed_line_node(0) is called and SPL1() is raised unconditionally (also when u_p == 0). It walks the stack from the top down re-linking nodes (UADD: unlink the range; UDEL: relink it; UMOV/VMOV: the pair is handled in one step), toggling each processed entry's type with ^= 1 (for a UMOV/VMOV pair only the lower entry's type is toggled), then reverses the order of the u_p entries, calls clear_active_list() if isglobal is set, exchanges current_addr with u_current_addr and addr_last with u_addr_last, calls SPL0() and returns 0.
note: checked oracle.c:538-583. Reviewer round 15 is right: the 'else if (u_p) modified = 1;' only guards modified; get_addressed_line_node(0) and SPL1 are unconditional. Round 2 (only lower UMOV/VMOV entry toggled) right and already in the old prose.

name: ref_exec_command
prose: Precondition: ibufp points at the command letter in the command buffer; addr_cnt, first_addr, second_addr, current_addr, addr_last and the editor state (isglobal, modified, scripted, errmsg, old_filename and the static substitution pattern state) are those of the command just parsed. Postcondition: reads one command letter after skipping blanks and runs that command. It returns ERR (with errmsg set by the command or its helpers) for the error cases of each command (bad address range, unexpected address or suffix, invalid destination, invalid pattern delimiter, no previous substitution, nested global command, unknown command, failed helper, crypt command 'x'), EMOD for 'e' on a modified buffer when not scripted, FATAL only for 'e'/'E' when close_sbuf succeeded but open_sbuf failed, and otherwise returns gflag: 0 for most commands, or the accumulated print-suffix bits (GPR/GLS/GNP from the p, l, n suffix) for commands such as a, c, d, i, j, m, t, which makes the caller print the current line; EOF for 'q'/'Q' (and for 'wq'/'wQ' unless the write left a modified non-scripted buffer, in which case EMOD, and for 'q' alone EMOD when the buffer is modified and not scripted). Errors do not guarantee the buffer is unchanged: for 'e'/'E' the buffer lines are deleted (delete_lines(1, addr_last)) and the undo stack cleared before close_sbuf/open_sbuf/read_file are tried, so those errors leave an emptied buffer; other commands that fail inside a helper may have already changed lines.
note: slice cut the head: real function is ref_exec_command (oracle.c:1873-2296); every return was checked against cases a to '='/'!'/newline and the final 'return gflag'. Old prose claimed ERR leaves the buffer unchanged or recoverable by undo; not true for e/E (lines 1928-1946).

name: ref_move_lines
prose: Precondition: first_addr..second_addr is a valid non-empty range of existing lines and addr is a destination in 0..addr_last that is not inside the range, i.e. addr < first_addr or addr >= second_addr (the caller 'm' checks this). Postcondition: SPL1() is called on entry and SPL0() before each return. If addr == first_addr - 1 or addr == second_addr nothing is relinked and no undo record is pushed; current_addr = second_addr. Otherwise two UMOV undo records are pushed with push_undo_stack and the lines are relinked after addr, and current_addr becomes addr + (second_addr - first_addr + 1) when addr < first_addr and addr otherwise. In both cases, if isglobal the moved lines are removed from the active node set, modified = 1 and the function returns 0. If either push_undo_stack call returns NULL, the function returns ERR after SPL0() without relinking; because push_undo_stack's failure path (realloc failure) clears and frees the whole undo stack, no UMOV record of this call remains, and current_addr, modified and the active set are unchanged.
note: checked oracle.c:2515-2554 and ref_push_undo_stack (oracle.c:531-560). Old prose said the first UMOV record stays after a second-push failure; push_undo_stack clears the entire stack on its failure path (lines 552-559), so that is wrong.

name: ref_copy_lines
prose: Precondition: first_addr..second_addr is a valid non-empty range of existing lines and addr is in 0..addr_last. Postcondition: current_addr is set to addr at the start. If first_addr <= addr < second_addr the lines first_addr..addr are copied first and then the lines originally at addr+1..second_addr; otherwise lines first_addr..second_addr are copied in order. Each copy is made under SPL1()/SPL0() around that single line: dup_line_node, add_line_node (inserts after current_addr and advances current_addr), then for the first copy push_undo_stack(UADD, current_addr, current_addr) and for later copies up->t is moved to the new line, then modified = 1. On success it returns 0 with current_addr = addr + (second_addr - first_addr + 1) and modified = 1, and one UADD record covers all inserted lines. If dup_line_node fails it calls SPL0() and returns ERR with the lines copied so far still inserted (current_addr at the last inserted line, or addr if none) and modified = 1 only if at least one line was completely processed. If push_undo_stack fails (only possible for the first copy) the line has already been inserted by add_line_node, current_addr has advanced, modified is not set by this call, the undo stack has been cleared by push_undo_stack's failure path, and the function returns ERR.
note: checked oracle.c:2556-2587. Reviewer round 1 (SPL1 per line, not on entry) already reflected; checked np re-fetch for the overlapping case at line 2568.

name: ref_get_marked_node_addr
prose: Precondition: n is a character code; the code uses islower((unsigned char)n), so values outside 0..255 are not valid inputs (a value whose low byte is a lowercase letter would pass the test and then index mark[] out of range). Postcondition: if n is not a lowercase letter it sets errmsg to "invalid mark character" and returns ERR. Otherwise it returns get_line_node_addr(mark[n - 'a']): the line number of the marked node when the node is in the buffer list; if the mark is unset (NULL) or the node is not in the list, get_line_node_addr walks the list, and when the buffer is non-empty it sets errmsg to "invalid address" and returns ERR; for an unset mark on an empty buffer it returns 0. No locks are taken and nothing is allocated or freed.
note: checked oracle.c:2645-2652 and ref_get_line_node_addr (oracle.c:978-990). Reviewer round 1 ('get_line_node_addr returns ERR without setting errmsg') is WRONG: line 986 sets errmsg = "invalid address". The old prose repeated that mistake and is corrected; the empty-buffer case returning 0 is new.

name: ref_exec_global
prose: Precondition: interact is 0 or 1 and gflag holds print-suffix flags; when interact is 0, ibufp addresses the rest of the global command (under BACKWARDS a lone newline gives the command 'p'). Postcondition: returns long. When interact is 0 it reads the command list with get_extended_line; if that fails it returns ERR before clear_undo_stack is called. Then clear_undo_stack() is called and the function loops over the active lines: it sets current_addr = get_line_node_addr(lp) and returns ERR (leaving the negative value in current_addr) if that is negative. In interactive mode it displays the line (return ERR if display_lines fails), reads a reply with get_tty_line (negative: returns ERR; zero: errmsg 'unexpected end-of-file', ERR); a lone newline skips the line; '&' reuses the saved command or, if there is none, sets errmsg 'no previous command' and returns ERR; otherwise it reads the command with get_extended_line (ERR on failure) and copies it into the static buffer ocmd, growing ocmdsz with REALLOC (on failure errmsg 'out of memory' and ERR). It then runs the command list on that line: for each command it calls extract_addr_range and exec_command, and a negative status from either (ERR, EMOD, FATAL, or EOF from 'q') is returned immediately; a positive status from exec_command is passed to display_lines, whose negative result is also returned. Remaining active lines are then not processed. If all active lines are done it returns 0.
note: checked oracle.c:704-765 and REALLOC (oracle.c:97-111). Reviewer round 15 is right: get_line_node_addr failure leaves current_addr negative (line 726). Round 2 (clear_undo_stack after get_extended_line) is right and stated; round 1 (get_line_node_addr failure return) right.

name: ref_kunsetenv
prose: Precondition: env is a valid NUL-terminated name pointer. Postcondition: calls kenv(KENV_UNSET, env, NULL, 0) and returns its result unchanged; it prints nothing and has no other effect in this function.
note: slice cut the head: real function is ref_kunsetenv (oracle.c:247-254).

name: ref_st_hash
prose: Precondition: name points to at least len readable bytes (len >= 0) and tabsz > 0 (the final key % tabsz divides by tabsz after conversion to unsigned int). Postcondition: if len exceeds MAXKEYLEN (128) only the last 128 bytes are used. The used bytes are consumed as steps = len/sizeof(u_int) chunks of sizeof(u_int) bytes copied into a u_int in memory order and added to key with unsigned wraparound, plus, if res = len % sizeof(u_int) is non-zero, a final chunk of the last res bytes zero-padded on the right (val = 0 first). It returns key % tabsz computed in unsigned arithmetic. The sum wraps modulo 2^32 before the reduction by tabsz. Nothing is allocated or modified outside local variables.
note: slice cut the head: real function is ref_st_hash(char *name, int len, int tabsz) (oracle.c:225-284). Old prose said the whole sum is taken modulo tabsz; actually the u_int sum wraps first.

name: ref_yylex
prose: Precondition: arith_buf points to a NUL-terminated string; if the next token is an identifier, the malloc behind stalloc succeeds (its result is not checked). Postcondition: calls oracle_init_is_type(), then skips ' ', '\t' and '\n' in a local pointer. It returns ARITH_BAD (4) without updating arith_buf, even if blanks were skipped, if the next character is not a recognised token start or is '+' or '-' immediately followed by the same character. At NUL it sets arith_buf to that NUL and returns 0. For a digit it stores strtoarith_t of the text in yylval.val (errno may be ERANGE), sets arith_buf past the number and returns ARITH_NUM (5). For a letter or '_' it stores a malloc'd NUL-terminated copy of the identifier in yylval.name (ownership passes to the caller), sets arith_buf past it and returns ARITH_VAR (6). Otherwise it returns the operator code, with arith_buf advanced past the token: '=' gives ARITH_ASS (1) or ARITH_EQ (12) for '=='; '||' ARITH_OR (2); '&&' ARITH_AND (3); '!' ARITH_NOT (7) or ARITH_NE (23) for '!='; '<' ARITH_LT (10), '<=' ARITH_LE (8), '<<' ARITH_LSHIFT (15), '<<=' ARITH_LSHIFTASS (26); '>' ARITH_GT (11), '>=' ARITH_GE (9), '>>' ARITH_RSHIFT (16), '>>=' ARITH_RSHIFTASS (27); '%' ARITH_REM (13) or ARITH_REMASS (24); '&' ARITH_BAND (14) or ARITH_BANDASS (25); '*' ARITH_MUL (17) or ARITH_MULASS (28); '+' ARITH_ADD (18) or ARITH_ADDASS (29); '|' ARITH_BOR (19) or ARITH_BORASS (30); '-' ARITH_SUB (20) or ARITH_SUBASS (31); '^' ARITH_BXOR (21) or ARITH_BXORASS (32); '/' ARITH_DIV (22) or ARITH_DIVASS (33); '(' ARITH_LPAREN (34); ')' ARITH_RPAREN (35); '~' ARITH_BNOT (36); '?' ARITH_QMARK (37); ':' ARITH_COLON (38). yylval is modified only for ARITH_NUM and ARITH_VAR.
note: checked oracle.c:236-432. Reviewer round 15 is WRONG: lines 402-411 return ARITH_BAD for '++' and '--' and no yylval is set for ADD/SUB. Round 2 (ASS, OR, AND codes) right and already in the prose. This record holds the head of the function; the same function is cut again in record 302-432.

name: main
prose: Precondition: none (the harness main takes no arguments). Postcondition: disables buffering on stdout, prints a header, runs every test_* routine listed in the function (getcomponent, savestr, nextfield, skipbl, readline, indent, main, parse_output, outsizes, outfunc, sigstring, printsignals, have_traps, preadateof, pungetc, each in hand and sweep forms where listed), then prints a table with one row per stats[] entry (function name, cases, failures) and a TOTAL row. It returns 1 if the total failure count is non-zero and 0 otherwise; this is its only return.
note: the listed name 'report' is not a function. Lines 1313-1323 are the tail of main() (harness.cpp:1279-1323). The first part of main only calls the test routines; checked 1281-1311.

name: ref___getcontextx_size
prose: Precondition: none. Postcondition: returns (int)(sizeof(ucontext_t) + sizeof(struct arm64_reg_context)) for the types defined in this oracle file. With these definitions compiled for x86_64 (gcc) sizeof(ucontext_t) is 960 and sizeof(struct arm64_reg_context) is 8, so it returns 968. It allocates nothing and modifies no state.
note: checked oracle.c:115-124; computed sizeof by compiling the oracle's type definitions with gcc on x86_64: 960 and 8. Reviewer round 1 (952) and round 15 (944+8) were both WRONG; the old prose's 968 was right.

name: tmp
prose: Precondition: none; reads TMPDIR with secure_getenv. Postcondition: formats "<TMPDIR or /tmp>/bt.XXXXXXXXXX" into a MAXPATHLEN buffer. If the formatted length is negative or does not fit it sets errno to ENAMETOOLONG and returns -1 before touching the signal mask. Otherwise it blocks all signals (saving the old mask), calls mkostemp(path, O_CLOEXEC), unlinks the path if mkostemp succeeded, restores the saved signal mask, and returns the descriptor from mkostemp, which is -1 (with errno as set by mkostemp) on failure.
note: checked oracle.c:1069-1091 (the file renames it ref_tmp with #define at line 738). Reviewer round 15 is right: the ENAMETOOLONG return happens before the mask is blocked.

name: ref___bt_stkacq
prose: Precondition: t is a valid btree with a buffer pool, *hp is a pinned page, c is the cursor with a key and cursor page number c->pg.pgno. Postcondition: returns 0 on success and 1 on failure. It first releases the page *hp (mpool_put) and runs __bt_search for c->key; if that returns NULL it returns 1 with *hp unchanged. If the page found has pgno == c->pg.pgno it skips to the exit. Otherwise it walks right along nextpg links, repairing the descent stack with BT_POP/BT_PUSH, and if the cursor page is still not found it re-runs __bt_search and walks left along prevpg links. Any mpool_get failure during the walks, or a failing __bt_search, returns 1 with *hp unchanged. When a walk ends (cursor page found, or no more neighbours) control reaches the exit, which releases the page it holds and sets *hp = mpool_get(c->pg.pgno): the function returns 0 if that fetch succeeds (even if the walks did not locate the cursor page) and returns 1 with *hp set to NULL if it fails. On success *hp is the cursor page, pinned, and the descent stack is the path of the last page visited (the cursor page itself is not pushed).
note: checked oracle.c:402-532 (record starts mid-file but head present). Reviewer round 1 right (exit reached even when the cursor page is not located); round 2 right (not pushed); round 15 right (*hp becomes NULL on final fetch failure).
